name: OpenRouter

auth.keyHelp: Create a key and set a credit limit so a leaked key cannot spend more than that; manage or delete keys at openrouter.ai/settings/keys.

read.label: Show this key's label, usage and limit
Show account credits (needs a management key)

write.label: Send a chat message to a model (billed per token)

tested: mock; real service refused a fake key
notes: Base URL https://openrouter.ai/api/v1 and Bearer auth are from the Authentication page; key creation page https://openrouter.ai/keys, manage/delete at https://openrouter.ai/settings/keys. KEY INFO: the Limits page says GET https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/key with a valid key returns data.label, limit, limit_reset, limit_remaining, include_byok_in_limit, budgets, effective_budget, usage (+ daily/weekly/monthly), byok_usage (+ periods), is_free_tier and free_model_daily_requests; rate_limit is deprecated. That page did not name the auth header (the Authentication page says Bearer). The older doc URL for the current-key endpoint returned 404 so the path /key comes from the Limits page only. data.label as 'who' is a key label, not an account name. GET /models: the OpenAPI-style page says auth is required via bearer token and returns data[], total_count and links.next (pricing as strings in USD per token). GET /credits needs a MANAGEMENT key (403 'Only management keys can perform this operation' otherwise) and returns data.total_credits and data.total_usage; a normal key will 403, so keep it out of the connection test. POST /chat/completions: the schema marks only messages as required (model optional there, but practically needed); billed against credits (402 on insufficient credits). Optional attribution headers: HTTP-Referer and X-OpenRouter-Title (the page examples use X-OpenRouter-Title, not X-Title); not set because they are the app's own choice. OAUTH: OpenRouter documents a PKCE flow that issues a normal API key without any client registration; localhost callbacks on any port are allowed (such apps get a host-and-port title and are left out of rankings). It is in signIn because it needs no client of the person's own. MCP: official remote server hosted by OpenRouter at https://mcp.openrouter.ai/mcp; OAuth with PKCE via a browser consent page which issues a dedicated key that expires in at most 7 days with a $10 starting spend cap that the person can edit. 17 tools; send-message and generate-image make billable calls, send-feedback writes feedback, the rest are read-only. A search result named other URLs (openrouter.ai/docs/_mcp/server); only the URL on the official MCP page was used. No call was made.
